clue.text: Second print, surprisingly featureless

indicators.note: signals that the letters of the two words come out in an unexpected new order

explanation.surface: A collector notices that a second printing of a book or stamp is disappointingly plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacking distinctive features is dull and hard to describe, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Fellow brought over makes slight bow

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning the word over reads it upwards, backwards

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A college fellow, arriving, gives a small bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick tilt of the head in greeting is a slight bow.

clue.text: Nick, bridge player, disheartened holding clubs

indicators.note: the trimmed player goes round the clubs letter
the word loses its heart, its middle letter

parts.note: the four bridge players are named by compass points
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A man named Nick, a bridge player, is downcast while holding clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name; it is a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A small V-shaped cut is a nick, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Welcome hug

definitions.meaning: to accept an idea eagerly, as in welcoming change
to hold someone in one's arms

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to accept gladly and to clasp someone in the arms.

clue.text: Ostrich up and running in pursuit

indicators.note: the letters are set running and land in a new order

explanation.surface: An ostrich is on its feet and sprinting after something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up and running' looks like a single idiom, but 'up' is part of the letters to be mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooing someone is the pursuit of a partner, the romantic sense of chasing.

clue.text: Country home — financial support needs to be raised

parts.note: being 'in' means being at home

indicators.note: in a down clue the support word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: aid is help, often in money

explanation.surface: A nation's domestic economy needs more funding.
explanation.definitionFit: The large South Asian republic is an example of a country.

clue.text: Sort of light craft following one to resort

indicators.note: re-sorting letters means rearranging them

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A light boat comes in behind another heading to a holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Signals at road junctions are a kind of light named after the vehicles they control.

clue.text: Dance step — last in quickstep, for instance

indicators.note: asks for the final letter of the word quickstep

parts.note: 'as' introduces an example, just like 'for instance'

explanation.surface: A dance teacher names a step, offering the end of a quickstep as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: In ballet the French term for a single step is borrowed directly into English.

clue.text: Mail includes recent article on Tory leader (copy)

indicators.note: in a down clue the article sits on top of the next letter
the mail word goes round the recent word

parts.note: post is mail
hot news is recent news
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: asks for the first letter of the word Tory

explanation.surface: A newspaper features a fresh piece about the Conservative leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail' suggests the Daily Mail; here it is simply the post.
explanation.definitionFit: The trade name for an old photographic copying machine came to mean a photocopy.

clue.text: Pull out ace, say —- this may win you instant cash

definitions.text: this may win you instant cash

parts.note: to scratch a horse is to withdraw it from a race
an ace is an example of a playing card

explanation.surface: A gambler is told to draw an ace for a quick payout.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery ticket whose panel one rubs off reveals at once whether it pays a prize.

clue.text: Legally obliged to limit tax to be laid out up front

indicators.text: to be laid out up front
indicators.note: tells us the tax word is placed at the front, before the limiting word

parts.note: a duty is a tax, as on imports
to bound something is to set a limit on it

explanation.surface: A legal instruction to cap a tax payable in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Being required by law or obligation to do something is an idiomatic synonym of being legally obliged.

clue.text: Love affair starts to anger my Oxford University roommates

indicators.note: asks for the opening letter of each of the following five words

explanation.surface: A student's romance begins to annoy the people sharing their college room.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for love is used in English for a romantic, often secret, liaison.

clue.text: Really try in a motorbike event

indicators.note: places the trying word inside the motorbike race

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
a judge hears a case, that is, tries it

explanation.surface: An invitation to have a real go at a motorcycle race.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the famous motorbike race held each year on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep down, in one's true nature, means really or fundamentally, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Fitting pocket

definitions.meaning: to take for oneself, often dishonestly

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means suitable; as a verb it means to take something for one's own use.

clue.text: Offend a fine head

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
the head of something is its front

explanation.surface: A quaint rebuke: a nice-looking head can cause offence.
explanation.definitionFit: To insult someone openly is to offend them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Bustle at university, revolutionary place of further education

parts.note: being 'up' is the old phrase for being in residence at university
LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.walkthrough: UP is reversed to PU by 'revolutionary'. The LSE is the London School of Economics, a university college in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To throb or stir with activity, as a lively city does, is a figurative sense matching bustle.

clue.text: Autobiography is economical with the truth about female politician

indicators.note: the lying word goes round the female letter

parts.note: a famous euphemism for telling lies
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A memoir that bends the truth about a woman in politics.
explanation.definitionFit: An autobiography is an account of one's own life written by oneself.

clue.text: Hard work put an end to child's play?

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
op is short for opus, a work
to scotch a rumour or plan is to put an end to it

explanation.surface: Someone tired of toil wonders whether stopping it would be easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'child's play' looks like the idiom for something easy, but here it means a literal children's game.
explanation.definitionFit: The hopping playground game marked out in chalked squares is literally a game children play.

clue.text: Hotel employee there, excited about topless girls

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A bellboy is thrilled by glamour models.

explanation.definitionFit: The British tabloid feature named after its page number was known for topless models, so the name stands for them.

clue.text: It's not on — leg on article's not made to measure

indicators.note: in an across clue, the leg word sits after the article word

parts.note: something cancelled or switched off is not on
'the' is the definite article
a peg is a slang word for a leg

explanation.definitionFit: Clothes bought ready-made from a rail rather than tailored are idiomatically described this way.

clue.text: That woman's name raised as no true believer

parts.note: her is the possessive for that woman

indicators.note: in a down clue the naming word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to cite is to name, as a source

explanation.surface: A woman's name is brought up as an unbeliever's.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone holding unorthodox beliefs against the church's doctrine is not a true believer.

clue.text: Not included in special edition

definitions.meaning: an additional charge is one not included in the price
a newspaper's special edition, issued beyond the regular ones

explanation.surface: Something left out of a limited-release version of a product.
explanation.definitionFit: An additional item lies outside what is included, and a newspaper's special issue bears the same name.

clue.text: Use former pilot, nervously

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: a nervous pilot fidgets, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Employ a retired airman who is jittery.

clue.text: Backing soldiers, play guitar on stage

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, soldiers who are not officers
to strum is to play a guitar by brushing the strings

explanation.surface: A performer supported by troops plays guitar during a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform for a speaker or performer is a kind of stage.

clue.text: A piece of cork in my French wine

indicators.note: puts the first pieces inside the French word

parts.note: mon is French for my

indicators.note: a piece of cork here is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bit of cork has fallen into a French wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A Burgundy town gives its name to the wines produced around it.

clue.text: Moved cautiously, giving warning to editor

parts.note: a tip-off is a warning

explanation.surface: A reporter crept about while tipping off the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking quietly on the balls of the feet is moving with care, a near synonym.

clue.text: A diamond ring turned up in the end

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a diamond is a gem
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A diamond ring finally reappears.

clue.text: On a spree

definitions.meaning: as in a book on birds, meaning concerning
a bout of drinking is a spree

explanation.definitionFit: The word means concerning, as 'on' can, and split in two it gives a session or binge.

clue.text: NCO taking in last of intake for physical

parts.note: a corporal is a non-commissioned officer

clue.text: Solution is extremely elegant, in part

indicators.note: only part of these words is taken, the letters across their junction

explanation.surface: A neat fix is very stylish, at least partly.

clue.text: See court painter beheaded

indicators.note: the painter's name loses its first letter, its head

clue.text: Focus on coin in box

indicators.note: places the first two pieces inside the box

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box
